title: City of Xenia - Ford Road WWTP
warnings: THE RECEIVING WATER IS NOT BLANK HERE (contrast with the mansfield precedent). Sheet 1's authorization sentence reads in full: "...discharge from the City of Xenia - Ford Road WWTP wastewater treatment works, located at 779 Ford Road, Xenia, Ohio, Greene County, to the Little Miami River at River Mile 77.03 in accordance with the conditions specified in Part I, II, and III, of this permit." Stream name and river mile are both present and read directly from that sentence; no recovery from Part II was needed for either.

THIS PERMIT HAS NO PHASE-IN AND NO SECOND LIMITED OUTFALL. Unlike the mansfield precedent (outfall 002 carrying Initial/Final tables with a 36/37-month toxicity phase-in), Xenia's Part I.A is ONE table, for the WHOLE permit term (2026-02-01 through 2031-01-31), at ONE outfall (001). Station 002 here is a bypass-only monitoring point (Part I.B.1) with no numeric effluent limits at all — see `bypass_002` below. There is nothing to diff.

PART I.C CARRIES A SINGLE MILESTONE, NOT A TOXICITY REDUCTION EVALUATION. The Fact Sheet (p.15) explains why: WET testing places Ford Road WWTP in "Category 4" — the plant's effluent does not currently pose a toxicity problem, so only continued annual monitoring is required, with no numeric acute/chronic toxicity limit and consequently no TRE schedule. The only Schedule of Compliance item is the Municipal Pretreatment local-limits justification, due 6 months after the effective date (event code 52599). See `schedule_of_compliance` below.

THE DISTRICT OFFICE IS NAMED CONSISTENTLY (contrast with the mansfield precedent, which named two different district offices for two schedules at the same facility). Both Part I.C.1.a (sheet 16) and Part II Item J (sheet 21-22) name the "Southwest District Office" — the pretreatment submittal and the selenium PEL notification both route there. No cross-part disagreement to flag.

STATION 588's TABLE CODE AND ITS OWN FOOTNOTE DISAGREE ON THE PARAMETER CODE. The Part I.B.5 monitoring table for station 1PD00015588 (sludge transferred to another NPDES permittee, sheet 11) lists parameter "51129 - Sludge Fee Weight." Footnote d on the SAME sheet reads: "...This value of percent total solids shall be used to calculate the total Sewage Sludge Weight (Discharge Monitoring Report code 70316) removed from the treatment plant on that day" — citing code 70316, which does not appear anywhere in the 588 table. 588 is the ONLY one of the three sludge-monitoring stations where table and footnote disagree: station 581 (sheets 8-9) prints BOTH codes in its own table (51129 and 70316) and its footnote f cites both together ("...code 70316) and/or total Sewage Sludge Fee Weight (Discharge Monitoring Report code 51129)..."); station 586 (sheet 10) prints only 51129 and its footnote d cites only 51129, matching its own table. 588 alone prints 51129 but has its footnote d cite 70316 instead — the real anomaly. Transcribed as printed at both places rather than silently reconciling; see `sludge_588` and `biosolids_581.also_monitored` below.

ONE PHOSPHORUS ROW HOLDS A CALCULATED VALUE UNDER A "MAXIMUM" HEADING. Part I.A footnote i (sheet 4) states outright that parameter 51451 ("Phosphorus, Total Load", printed with a "maximum" of 6.8 kg) "is actually a calculated annual average loading in 'kilograms' calculated during the summer months of May-October only although it is listed under a maximum concentration limit" — entered once, in November, via the Item Y calculation. The document is explicit that its own column header for this row is a formatting artifact, not a true daily maximum. Transcribed with that caveat attached rather than as an ordinary limit.

STATION 002's SAMPLING-STATION DESCRIPTION CARRIES TWO COORDINATE PAIRS, NOT ONE. Part II Item B (sheet 18) describes 1PD00015002 as: "Influent bypass from retention basin at (Lat/Long: 39.7119, -83.9652) prior to combining with final effluent at (Lat/Long: 39.7126, -83.9672) and ultimately discharging to the Little Miami River at Station 1PD00015001." Those are two distinct points in the process train (the bypass diversion itself, and the post-blending point), both printed inside one station's row. Both are transcribed under `sampling_stations.'1PD00015002'` rather than picking one.

NO DMS-TO-DECIMAL CONVERSION WAS NEEDED. Unlike the mansfield precedent, this permit prints its sampling-station coordinates already in decimal degrees ("Lat/Long: 39.7164, -83.9700"), not DMS. The values below are transcribed as printed, unconverted.

bypass_002.description: Treatment plant's bypass — monitored WHEN DISCHARGING; carries NO numeric limits (contrast with mansfield's 602, which had real TSS/CBOD limits)
bypass_002.note_e: "Discharge through this station is prohibited. The Director may take enforcement action for violations of this prohibition unless the three conditions specified at 40 CFR 122.41(m) and in Part III, Item M.3.a of this permit are met." As printed — the bypass station is monitored and reported in full even though bypass itself remains formally prohibited absent the CFR conditions.
bypass_002.no_numeric_trigger_in_the_permit_itself: Unlike the mansfield precedent (a printed "sustained peak flow of 19 MGD" precondition on its bypass station), NOTHING in this permit's own text sets a numeric flow threshold for when Ford Road's bypass may divert. The only such figure — "influent is diverted to the EQ basin when the flow exceeds 4 MGD" — appears in the bound Fact Sheet's Facility Description (p.6), which is NOT part of Parts I/II/III and is not itself an enforceable permit condition. See `fact_sheet_context.facility_description` below.

sso_300.note: As at mansfield, the permit is explicit that 1/Month is a REPORTING frequency, not a monitoring one: "the intent of that provision is to specify a reporting frequency for Overflow Occurrence, not a monitoring frequency... these overflows shall be monitored on each day when they discharge." Only SSOs reaching waters of the state (directly or through a storm sewer) are reported at this station; a multi-location day counts multiply.
sso_300.annual_report: An annual SSO report covering ALL overflows in the collection system (including those never reaching waters of the state) is due March 31 for the prior calendar year, with locations numbered consecutively from 301, volumes in millions of gallons, and a narrative WIB (water-in-basement) analysis by location, frequency and cause. Public notice of the report's availability is required (Part II Item C).

parameter_tracking_selenium.text: A preliminary effluent limit (PEL) tracking condition, not a numeric limit. The permittee must report to Ohio EPA Southwest District Office, in writing, within 30 days, any effluent result exceeding the PEL, and must reduce discharge levels below the PEL if the maximum PEL is exceeded four or more months, or the 30-day average PEL is exceeded two or more months, within any consecutive six-month period.
parameter_tracking_selenium.significance: Matches the Fact Sheet's own account (p.13-14): selenium sits in "group 4" — PEQ ≥ 50 percent but < 100 percent of the PEL — which under OAC 3745-33-07(A)(2) requires exactly this tracking condition rather than a numeric limit.

Ambient/upstream testing at station 801 in conjunction with the effluent tests. fact_sheet_context.citation_style: Fact Sheet for NPDES Permit Renewal, City of Xenia – Ford Road WWTP, 2025, page N of 35

facility_description.text: "The Ford Road WWTP was constructed in 1970 and last upgraded in 1999. The average design flow is 3.6 million gallons per day (MGD)... serves the north side of Xenia." Treatment train: influent pumping/screening, grit removal, flow equalization, activated sludge aeration with biological phosphorus removal, secondary clarification, ultraviolet disinfection. Sludge train: aerobic digestion, lime stabilization, mechanical dewatering; treated sludge is land applied.
facility_description.eq_basin_and_bypass_trigger: "The Ford Road WWTP has the ability to divert influent flow at the head of the plant to a 0.278-million-gallon flow equalization (EQ) basin. In general, influent is diverted to the EQ basin when the flow exceeds 4 MGD. When the EQ basin becomes full, wastewater discharges through an emergency overflow (outfall 002) without treatment. The untreated wastewater from outfall 002 combines with the final effluent, and the combined effluent discharges directly to the Little Miami River at outfall 001." This is the ONLY place any numeric bypass trigger appears in this document — see `bypass_002.no_numeric_trigger_in_the_permit_itself` above.
facility_description.infiltration_inflow_rate: "[T]he city of Xenia estimates there is an infiltration/inflow (I/I) rate to the collection system of 0.75 MGD." (Fact Sheet p.7, not p.6 — see the page note on `separated_sewers` below.) Mitigation measures listed: sliplining of sanitary lines, televising sewers for potential repairs, rehabilitation of manholes, smoke testing for illegal connections.
facility_description.separated_sewers: "The City of Xenia has 100% separated sewers... There are no combined sewers in the collection system for the Ford Road WWTP." (Fact Sheet p.7 — this block's own `page: 6` header covers only the construction/design-flow/treatment-train and EQ-basin text above; separated_sewers, significant_industrial_users and infiltration_inflow_rate are one page later.)
facility_description.significant_industrial_users: "The City of Xenia has two significant industrial users in their pretreatment program. Neither of these categorical industrial users are within the Ford Road WWTP collection area." (Fact Sheet p.7, same as separated_sewers above.)
